title: Sell Mineral Rights in Jefferson County, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Jefferson County, AL
metaDescription: Own mineral or royalty rights in Jefferson County, Alabama? We buy Black Warrior Basin coalbed methane interests with a clear, patient, honest offer.
heroLead: Jefferson County sits inside the Black Warrior Basin's coalbed methane fairway, and few counties in Alabama carry as long or as layered a mineral-ownership history, coal, iron, steel, and now natural gas, all stacked on the same land over more than a century.
intro: If you hold a mineral or royalty interest connected to Jefferson County, from Birmingham's old industrial core out to the smaller communities like Fairfield, Gardendale, Hueytown, or McCalla, you are sitting on a piece of one of the most heavily documented, and heavily severed, mineral estates in the state. We buy these interests, and we approach every one of them the way a family office would look at any other asset: understand it fully, weigh a lump sum against the after-tax present value of what remains, and only move forward when the numbers and your goals actually line up.
This page is meant to give you a real picture of what owning minerals in this county typically involves, not a sales pitch.

sections.heading: How this county's mineral estate got so fractured
paragraphs: Jefferson County's coal, iron ore, and later natural gas history means the same parcel of land was often leased, mined, sold, and re-leased multiple times across different eras and by different industries. Coal companies acquired large tracts in the late 1800s and early 1900s, then subdivided or sold off surface rights over the decades while various mineral rights stayed reserved in the chain of title. When coalbed methane development picked up in the 1980s and 1990s, operators went back through this same layered history to lease the gas rights specifically, sometimes from the coal-era mineral owner, sometimes from an heir several generations removed from whoever originally struck the deal.

The result is a county where a huge number of owners hold small fractional interests, an eighth, a sixteenth, a sixty-fourth, split among cousins who may not even know each other, all tracing back to one original tract. If that describes your situation, it is the norm here, not the exception.

sections.heading: The Black Warrior Basin coalbed methane picture
paragraphs: The core of Alabama's coalbed methane production sits in the Pottsville coal measures, the same Mary Lee, Blue Creek, and Pratt coal groups that were mined underground for generations before operators realized the methane trapped in those seams could be produced on its own. Western Jefferson County, along the Tuscaloosa County line near McCalla and Holt, sits closer to some of the basin's more established producing units, while the county's eastern and southern suburbs, Leeds, Hoover, Homewood, generally sit further from active development.

Energen Resources was historically the dominant operator across much of this coalbed methane fairway. Diversified Energy acquired that legacy portfolio and now operates a large share of the older, mature wells across Jefferson County, meaning many owners today receive statements from a company name that did not exist when the original lease was signed. That is normal, not a sign anything has gone wrong with your title.

These wells are mostly well past their peak. Coalbed methane production in this basin tends to decline gradually rather than sharply, which means owners often see small, steady checks for many years rather than a dramatic payout followed by a cliff. That steadiness is exactly why converting the remaining stream into one lump sum is worth evaluating for owners who have a specific use for the cash today.

sections.heading: Probate, heirs, and clearing title in Jefferson County
paragraphs: Jefferson County is unusual in Alabama in that it operates two probate court divisions, one based in Birmingham and one in Bessemer, depending on where in the county the estate was originally opened. If you inherited a mineral interest and are not sure which division holds the relevant file, that is one of the first things we help owners sort out.

Because so many of these interests have passed through two, three, or even four generations without formal estate administration at every step, heirs' property situations are common here. You may co-own an undivided interest with siblings, cousins, or more distant relatives you have never met, some of whom may not even know the interest exists. We can buy your specific undivided share without requiring every co-owner to participate, and where a family wants to sell together, we can coordinate that too.

In cases where title has never been formally cleared through probate, an heirship affidavit is often enough to establish your ownership without a lengthy court process, though every situation is different and we will tell you honestly what your specific case requires before you spend time or money on it.

sections.heading: What actually drives value for a Jefferson County interest
paragraphs: We weigh current or recent production against your net decimal interest, the maturity and decline stage of the specific well or unit, and how close your tract sits to active development versus the county's quieter edges. Two interests of identical acreage can be worth meaningfully different amounts depending on these factors, so we never quote off acreage alone.

Value talk in this business should always be hedged against real, current numbers rather than promises. What your interest is worth today depends on recent royalty statements, current natural gas prices, and how the specific well is performing, and any honest buyer will tell you that up front rather than quote a fixed price before looking at your documentation.

faqs.question: How do I know which town or unit my Jefferson County interest is tied to?
faqs.answer: The legal description on your deed or division order, section, township, and range, tells us exactly where your interest sits, and we can trace that against current well and unit records for you.

faqs.question: My statements come from Diversified Energy but my grandparent's paperwork mentions Energen. What happened?
faqs.answer: Diversified Energy acquired Energen's Black Warrior Basin coalbed methane portfolio, so this is a normal operator transition that does not affect your underlying ownership.

faqs.question: Do I need to go through probate before I can sell?
faqs.answer: If the interest passed through an estate that was never formally administered, you will likely need to clear that first, sometimes through full probate and sometimes through a simpler heirship affidavit depending on your circumstances.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Birmingham and Bessemer probate divisions?
faqs.answer: Jefferson County splits probate jurisdiction geographically, so which division holds your family's estate file depends on where in the county the property or the deceased owner was located.

faqs.question: Can multiple heirs sell their shares separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, each heir can sell their own undivided interest independently, and we regularly work with families where only some members choose to sell right away.

faqs.question: Should I talk to a CPA before selling?
faqs.answer: It is worth understanding the tax treatment of a mineral sale versus continued royalty income for your specific situation, and we would encourage you to run the numbers past your own CPA or tax advisor as part of deciding what is right for you.
